title: Breakfast Nachos Supreme
subtitle: Tortilla chips loaded with eggs, bacon, cheese, and salsa on sheet pans.
description: Tortilla chips loaded with scrambled eggs, sausage, cheese, and salsa on a sheet pan. Messy in the best way — serve with hot sauce and let the crew dig in.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Breakfast Nachos Supreme in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Bacon. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Prep components
steps.instruction: Cook bacon until crisp and crumble. Soft-scramble eggs—they should still look glossy. Warm nacho cheese. Drain pico thoroughly so chips don't sog out.

steps.title: Layer the chips
steps.instruction: Spread chips on two rimmed sheet pans in a single thick layer. Drizzle half the nacho cheese, then scatter half the shredded cheeses over each pan.

steps.title: First melt
steps.instruction: Bake at 400°F until cheese melts and chips at the edges toast lightly. Remove and distribute scrambled eggs and bacon evenly across both pans. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Broil to finish
steps.instruction: Add remaining cheese and broil on high 2–3 minutes until bubbling and spotty golden. Watch constantly—chips burn fast under the broiler.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Breakfast Nachos Supreme onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Top and serve
steps.instruction: Add pico, avocado, sour cream, and jalapeños immediately. Serve straight from the sheet pans at the line with extra hot sauce on the side.

stationWorkflow: Build on two pans so the crew can attack from both ends of the table without a traffic jam.
Hold avocado and sour cream cold until the nachos leave the broiler—hot chips wilt them fast.
Serve within 5 minutes of broiling; nachos don't hold, so call the crew as soon as pans hit the counter.
cleanupNotes: Line sheet pans with foil for easier cleanup after melted cheese and queso bond to the metal.
Discard soggy bottom chips rather than scraping—foil lift-and-toss is faster on busy mornings.
leftovers: Nachos don't reheat well; repurpose leftover toppings into breakfast burritos with fresh tortillas.
Use extra scrambled eggs and bacon in a hash with diced potatoes for the next shift.
